text: The AI screening has placed this study in a borderline set that includes both the 'No Tumour' category and one of the tumour categories. A 'No Tumour' output indicates that the model did not detect features it associates with the three tumour classes it was trained on [neurasight-system]. This occurs because the model only distinguishes among glioma, meningioma, pituitary tumour and a generic 'No Tumour' label, and any abnormality outside those four patterns can be forced into the latter class [nci-cns-pdq-patient]. Consequently, the system cannot definitively exclude a tumour when the probability distribution straddles the decision threshold, and the result should not be taken as a clean bill of health [nci-cns-pdq-patient]. Clinical symptoms such as sudden severe headache, new seizure activity, rapid visual change or loss of consciousness remain urgent signs irrespective of the AI output [ninds-brain-tumors]. It is therefore advisable to discuss with a qualified clinician the need for a full neurological examination, formal radiological review of the complete study and, if appropriate, repeat or additional imaging to resolve the uncertainty [nci-cns-pdq-patient] [ninds-brain-tumors].
